sources.title: Human History Map: French Indo-China imported record and decoded outlines
sources.note: Own-project factual source. Exact ID 1920 to 1938; world-1920 and world-1930 bounds 100,10.314,107.513,22.533. Point tests include Phnom Penh, Vientiane, Luang Prabang and Angkor; exclude Hanoi, Hue and Saigon. Separate Annam and Cochin China records occupy Vietnamese territory. No alias associations proposed.

sources.title: University of Perpignan, Digithèque MJP: decrees organizing French Indochina, 1887 and 1911
sources.note: Original university-hosted transcription verified in indexed full text; direct fetch timed out. 1887 report explains shared political, military, judicial, postal and customs services; 1911 articles 1 to 6 enumerate colony, protectorates, leased territory and governor-general powers. Introduction explains Laos in 1893.

sources.title: National Museum of Cambodia: Museum History
sources.note: Institutional original indexed text read. Museum opening 13 April 1920, school association, Cambodian students/artisans/teachers, 1951 handover. The page gives inconsistent school founding dates, so no exact school founding year is asserted.

sources.title: Harriet Winifred Ponder, Cambodian Glory (1936), The Tree of Knowledge: reproduced excerpt, part 1
sources.note: Primary visitor account reproduced in full selected excerpt. Doors: eight master craftsmen and ten pupils, 45 days. Read critically: do not adopt the author’s colonial rescue narrative or dismissive description of local people. Parts 1 and 2 count as one underlying work.

sources.title: Harriet Winifred Ponder, Cambodian Glory (1936), The Tree of Knowledge: reproduced excerpt, part 2
sources.note: Direct selected original excerpt read. Entry at fifteen, drawing then craft training; named craft categories; woman weaving teacher and approximate fortnight for one small sampot; wax models for bronze casting. Not a statistical account of all Cambodian children.

sources.title: Yale HRAF: Karl Gustav Izikowitz, Lamet: Hill Peasants in French Indochina (1951), source assessment
sources.note: Direct HRAF source abstract and fieldwork metadata read; not full subscription book. May 1937 to January 1938, northern Laos. Abstract supports swidden rice, labor exchange, households, extended families and religious calendar. Avoid numerical fallow-cycle claim because abstract wording could be misread.

sources.title: Geoffrey C. Gunn, Rebellion in Laos: Peasant and Politics in a Colonial Backwater
sources.note: Selected original indexed paragraph verified: administration undertook public works using corvee in 1934, roads and river communications; 1935 accounts discuss economic conditions and population noncooperation. Full PDF too large for web extraction; do not claim full-book review.

sources.title: Søren Ivarsson, Cultural Nationalism in a Colonial Context, in Recherches nouvelles sur le Laos, pp. 237 to 258
sources.note: Original institutional PDF downloaded; selected printed pp. 247 to 250 read from extracted text (PDF pp. 249 to 252). Phetsarath, Sila Viravong, Buddhist institutes in Phnom Penh 1930, Vientiane 1931 and Luang Prabang 1933; political objective of redirecting links away from Siam. Not a whole-volume certification.

sources.title: Gracie Lee, Early Printing in Indochina, National Library Singapore, BiblioAsia (2020)
sources.note: Full institutional article read. Laos section: 1930s printed stories recopied onto palm leaves; Sila Viravong four-volume grammar in 1935; Cambodia section: Khmer types and vernacular publication. PDF mirror is the same work.

sources.title: ISEAS Yusof Ishak Institute Library: The First Women’s Newspapers in Vietnam
sources.note: Direct institutional article read, especially Phụ Nữ Tân Văn section. Gives exact original title and English gloss Women’s Gazette, first issue 2 May 1929, Thursday publication, women’s education/career advocacy and cover depicting readers from three Vietnamese regions. Cover image not independently visually opened; no exact issue-85 date used because caption appears questionable.

sources.title: Institut Pasteur: Du vaccin contre la rage à la création de l’Institut
sources.note: Direct institutional history read. 1891 Saigon under Albert Calmette, rabies and smallpox mission; Phnom Penh veterinary annex 1946 and institute December 1953. Keep locations and later dates explicit.

sources.title: Marc Jason Gilbert, interview with historian Michael G. Vann, World History Connected 15.2 (2018)
sources.note: Direct interview with original archival researcher read. Hanoi sewers, 1902 rat-kill records, tail bounty, tailless rats, farms and trade. The 1902 example predates this atlas window; not invented humor or a claim that every dwelling had a sewer connection.

sources.title: Lao PDR nomination dossier: Megalithic Jar Sites in Xiengkhuang, UNESCO document 166326
sources.note: Original indexed passage checked: official monuments inventory 1926; Colani work and funerary interpretation reported 1932; pots, ornaments and beads. Full PDF web open rejected for size. Evidence of colonial-period research on much earlier sites, not construction by the colonial government.

sources.title: University of Perpignan, Digithèque MJP: French Indochina, 1945 to 1954
sources.note: University original indexed full introduction read; direct fetch timed out. Japanese military presence alongside Vichy administration from 1940, coup 9 March 1945, French return, war 1946, Cambodian full independence 9 November 1953, Geneva July 1954. Do not repeat French government’s self-justifying declarations as neutral fact.

sources.title: University of Perpignan, Digithèque MJP: Franco-Lao treaty of 22 October 1953
sources.note: University original indexed introduction and treaty articles read. Distinguishes 1949 associated-state status from full sovereignty under article 1 in 1953; continued French Union association article 2. Direct fetch timed out.

proposedOverrides.name: French Indo-China
proposedOverrides.summary: A colonial federation whose 1920 to 1938 atlas outline mainly covers Laos and Cambodia.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct card, no aliases. Historical federation and component territories separated; current atlas polygon is narrower than the name.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Both sampled polygons exclude major Vietnamese cities while including Lao and Cambodian capitals. The 1920 to 1938 range is map coverage, not the life of the federation.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Phụ Nữ Tân Văn, Women’s Gazette; original Vietnamese Roman script, Saigon newspaper founded 2 May 1929. Institutional text witness verified, image not independently inspected.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Ponder parts 1 and 2 grouped as one work. HRAF only source abstract read; Gunn and UNESCO selected indexed originals. University decree/treaty reproductions verified indexed, direct fetch timed out. No fabricated universal schooling, toilet access or family customs.
